Arthur Conan Doyle, The Sign of the Four.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/arthur-conan-doyle/the-sign-of-the-four

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Arthur Conan Doyle, the author, died 1930.

First publication of the text used: February 1890, in Lippincott's Monthly Magazine (United States) (Wikipedia). The British book followed in October 1890 (Spencer Blackett, United Kingdom), and British journals republished the novel in the months after. SE colophon: 'The Sign of the Four was published in 1890 by Arthur Conan Doyle.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in the United States in February 1890, before 1931, so it is in the public domain in the United States.
- Country of origin: the first publication was in the United States (Lippincott's Monthly Magazine, February 1890), so the country of origin is the United States, and the United States rule above settles it whatever the death year. The United Kingdom publications came after the first United States publication, not at the same time.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
